repo_notes.author: Korben
repo_notes.content: This repository is a fork of godotengine/godot tracking upstream `master`. The engine version is defined in `version.py` (currently 4.7-beta); always derive the engine version from `version.py`, never from demo-project files. References to 'Godot 4.3+' in `steel_streets/README.md` and `steel_streets/project.godot` describe the minimum editor version for that demo game only, not the engine version of this repo. The only fork-specific addition is the top-level `steel_streets/` Godot project (a Game Boy-style GDScript demo game); everything else mirrors upstream, so upstream docs (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest) apply.

repo_notes.author: Korben
repo_notes.content: Architecture layering to use throughout the wiki: `core/` (Object/ClassDB, Variant, memory, I/O, ProjectSettings, GDExtension interface in `core/extension/`, profiling in `core/profiling/`) -> `servers/` (RenderingServer, RenderingDevice, DisplayServer + AccessibilityServer, physics_2d/3d, navigation_2d/3d, audio, text, xr, camera, movie_writer, debugger) -> `scene/` (SceneTree, Node, Viewport/Window, gui, 2d, 3d, animation, resources) -> `editor/`. `drivers/` holds graphics/audio/OS backends (vulkan, d3d12, metal, gles3, accesskit, sdl, alsa/pulseaudio, wasapi, coreaudio). `platform/` holds OS ports: linuxbsd (X11 and Wayland), windows, macos, ios, visionos, android, web. `modules/` holds optional features (gdscript, mono, jolt_physics, godot_physics_2d/3d, navigation_2d/3d, openxr, webxr, gltf, fbx, text_server_adv/fb, lightmapper_rd, multiplayer, etc.). `thirdparty/` is vendored code and should only be described at a high level (see `thirdparty/README.md`), never documented file-by-file.

repo_notes.author: Korben
repo_notes.content: Recent upstream changes the wiki must reflect (4.6 -> 4.7 cycle): HDR output support across Windows, macOS (Metal and Vulkan), and Linux Wayland (`display/window/hdr/request_hdr_output` project setting, `DisplayServer.window_is_hdr_output_supported`, HDR luminance APIs, notifications when HDR state changes externally); new rectangular `AreaLight3D` (`AreaLight3D` in `scene/3d/light_3d.h`, `LIGHT_AREA` in `servers/rendering/rendering_server_enums.h`) across renderers; Wayland touch support; reworked export template manager allowing individual template installs and TPZ installs (`editor/export/export_template_manager.*`); the editor Asset Library reworked into the Asset Store and ported to the new store API (`editor/asset_library/`); Perfetto tracing hooks in `core/profiling/` (on by default for Android debug builds); GDExtension additions such as `classdb_register_extension_class6` / `classdb_construct_object3` and `RequiredParam`/`RequiredResult`; new projects default to `canvas_items` stretch mode with `expand` aspect (set in `editor/editor_node.cpp`); `Object::is_class` takes `StringName`.

repo_notes.author: Korben
repo_notes.content: Developer workflow facts for this team's environment: SCons >= 4.0 and Python >= 3.9 (enforced in `SConstruct`). Standard dev build: `scons tests=yes target=editor dev_build=yes -j$(nproc)` producing `bin/godot.linuxbsd.editor.dev.x86_64`; linking needs roughly 8 GB RAM (swap may be required). Unit tests use doctest under `tests/` and run with `./bin/godot.linuxbsd.editor.dev.x86_64 --headless --test`, filtered with `--test-case="*Name*"`; new test files can be scaffolded with `tests/create_test.py`. Linting/formatting is via pre-commit (`.pre-commit-config.yaml`: clang-format, clang-tidy, ruff, mypy, codespell, dotnet-format, eslint, header-guard/copyright/file-format checks). CI is GitHub Actions: `.github/workflows/runner.yml` runs static_checks then per-platform build workflows. `CONTRIBUTING.md` requires AI agents to self-disclose (robot emoji prefix in PR/issue title plus an AI disclosure note in the description) - document this in the contribution workflow page.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to the Godot Engine codebase: purpose, engine version (from version.py), directory map (core, servers, scene, editor, drivers, platform, modules, thirdparty, tests, doc, main) and how the layers depend on each other. Mention the fork-specific steel_streets demo project.

pages.title: Building from Source (SCons)
pages.purpose: Document SConstruct, methods.py, platform detect.py files, key build options (target, dev_build, tests, precision, module_*_enabled, scu_build, sanitizers, linker), output binary naming, and local build/test commands.

page_notes.content: Include the team's standard command `scons tests=yes target=editor dev_build=yes -j$(nproc)` and the ~8 GB link memory requirement.

pages.title: Core Engine
pages.purpose: Document core/: Object, ClassDB and method binding, signals, RefCounted, Variant and containers, StringName, memory management, OS/threads/WorkerThreadPool, and main/ startup sequence.

pages.title: Resources, I/O and ProjectSettings
pages.purpose: Document Resource loading/saving, ResourceUID, FileAccess/DirAccess, PCK packs, ProjectSettings and core/config.

pages.title: Scene System
pages.purpose: Document SceneTree main loop, Node lifecycle and notifications, groups, PackedScene/SceneState serialization and instancing.

pages.title: Node Tree, Viewport and Window
pages.purpose: Document Viewport, Window, SubViewport, input propagation, embedded windows, stretch modes (new-project default canvas_items/expand) and HDR-related Window properties.

pages.title: GUI Controls and Text
pages.purpose: Document Control layout/theme system, containers, PopupMenu, Tree, Label, LineEdit, TextEdit/CodeEdit, RichTextLabel and their interaction with TextServer.

pages.title: 2D, 3D Nodes and Animation
pages.purpose: Document scene/2d and scene/3d node families (cameras, lights incl. AreaLight3D, meshes, GridMap, skeleton modifiers such as SpringBoneSimulator3D) and scene/animation (AnimationPlayer, AnimationTree, blend trees).

pages.title: Servers Architecture
pages.purpose: Explain the server pattern (RID-based APIs, thread-safe wrappers via server_wrap_mt_common.h, register_server_types) and list every server in servers/.

pages.title: Rendering Architecture
pages.purpose: Document RenderingServer, RenderingDevice and its graph, the Forward+ (forward_clustered), Mobile (forward_mobile) and Compatibility (drivers/gles3) renderers, shader language/compiler, and effects.

page_notes.content: Cover AreaLight3D/LIGHT_AREA support and screen-space AA/FSR/MetalFX scaling behavior on Mobile.

pages.title: Graphics Drivers
pages.purpose: Document RenderingDeviceDriver backends: Vulkan, D3D12, Metal, plus the GLES3 driver and shader container/baking.

pages.title: HDR Output
pages.purpose: Document end-to-end HDR output: request_hdr_output project setting, DisplayServer/Window HDR APIs, RenderingDevice SUPPORTS_HDR_OUTPUT feature, and per-platform implementations (Windows, macOS Metal/Vulkan, Wayland) including change notifications.

pages.title: Display Server, Input and Accessibility
pages.purpose: Document DisplayServer abstraction, windows, IME, native menus, input events and joypads (SDL driver), headless mode, and AccessibilityServer with the AccessKit driver.

pages.title: Physics (GodotPhysics and Jolt)
pages.purpose: Document PhysicsServer2D/3D APIs, godot_physics_2d/3d modules, the jolt_physics module, physics command queue, and how the engine is selected in project settings.

pages.title: Audio, Navigation and XR
pages.purpose: Document AudioServer and audio drivers, NavigationServer2D/3D with the navigation_2d/3d modules, and XRServer with openxr/webxr/mobile_vr modules.

pages.title: Text Server
pages.purpose: Document TextServer API and text_server_adv (HarfBuzz/ICU) vs text_server_fb backends, fonts and shaping.

pages.title: Scripting and GDScript
pages.purpose: Document the ScriptLanguage/ScriptInstance abstraction and the GDScript module: tokenizer, parser, analyzer, compiler, VM, warnings, and language server.

pages.title: C# / .NET (Mono Module)
pages.purpose: Document modules/mono: glue generation, GodotSharp assemblies, build integration and editor support.

pages.title: GDExtension
pages.purpose: Document core/extension: GDExtensionManager, interface headers, extension_api.json dump, class registration versions (e.g. classdb_register_extension_class6), RequiredParam/RequiredResult and compatibility with godot-cpp.

pages.title: Modules and Third-Party Libraries
pages.purpose: Explain the module system (config.py, SCsub, register_types) with a categorized overview of modules/, and summarize vendored libraries in thirdparty/ at a high level.

pages.title: Platform Ports
pages.purpose: Document platform/ ports (linuxbsd X11/Wayland, windows, macos, ios, visionos, android, web): OS/DisplayServer implementations, export plugins, and platform-specific build notes.

pages.title: Editor Architecture
pages.purpose: Document EditorNode, docks, inspector, undo/redo, EditorSettings, project manager and editor themes.

pages.title: Scene Editors and Plugins
pages.purpose: Document EditorPlugin/EditorInterface, 2D/3D viewports, GridMap/TileMap, animation, script and shader editors.

pages.title: Import, Export and Asset Store
pages.purpose: Document the import pipeline (editor/import, glTF/FBX), export presets and platforms, the reworked export template manager, and the new Asset Store in editor/asset_library.

pages.title: Debugger and Profilers
pages.purpose: Document script debugger, remote scene tree, visual/frame profilers, ObjectDB profiler and Perfetto tracing hooks in core/profiling.

pages.title: Development Workflow
pages.purpose: Document how to contribute: branching, PR conventions, CONTRIBUTING.md rules (including the AI-agent self-disclosure requirement), and pre-commit hooks.

pages.title: Test Suite
pages.purpose: Document doctest-based tests under tests/, test_main.cpp, test macros, create_test.py, running and filtering tests, and Python build tests in tests/python_build.

pages.title: CI, Documentation and Code Style
pages.purpose: Document GitHub Actions workflows (runner.yml, static_checks, per-platform builds), doc/classes XML class reference and make_rst, clang-format/clang-tidy/ruff style rules.

pages.title: Steel Streets Demo Game
pages.purpose: Document the fork-specific steel_streets/ Godot project: 160x144 Game Boy-style viewport and palette, GameManager autoload, player/enemy/boss scripts, scene flow (splash, title, level, game over, victory), input map, and the tools/gen_assets.py asset generator.

page_notes.content: This is a standalone GDScript game project run with `godot --path steel_streets`; it is not part of the engine build.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.purpose: Define key engine terms (RID, ClassDB, Variant, SceneTree, Viewport, RenderingDevice, Forward+, GDExtension, AccessKit, HDR output, Jolt, etc.) with links to source locations.
